evals.prompt: I'm picking this AEMS project back up after a few months away — it's the kayaking competition scoring app. From what I remember: there's a FastAPI backend that owns all the scoring and competition data, and a React frontend that judges use on tablets. The frontend and backend talk directly to each other, and I think we're using plain WebSockets for the live score updates since we rolled our own reconnect logic for that ages ago. The frontend just calls the backend's REST endpoints directly for everything else — no code generation or anything like that. I don't remember there being anything besides those two services. Can you check whether that's still an accurate picture of how the system is put together? Repo is at C:\Users\anton\CodeInSight-eval-targets\AEMS.
evals.expected_output: A reality-check report (architecture/C4 lens) saved under docs/mental-model/ in the AEMS repo, with a plain 'your model' diagram matching the two-service description given, and a graded 'reality' C4 diagram. Should grade the WebSockets claim red (actually Socket.IO per ADR006), the 'no code generation' claim red (aemsApi.ts is generated from OpenAPI via buildApi.sh), 'React frontend' amber (it's Next.js), the FastAPI/scoring ownership claim green, and flag GraphicsServer/Timer/Common as grey (real but unmentioned).
